entries.title: Stripe checkout with webhooks and idempotency keys
entries.description: Checkout sessions, signed webhooks and idempotency keys, in the order a builder writes them.
entries.source: Written up from a retry pair on Spring launch site, M3
entries.content:
## When to use it
Any checkout that takes a card through Stripe.

## Worked example
```ts src/lib/checkout.ts
const key = `checkout:${cart.id}:${cart.version}`;
const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create(
  { mode: "payment", line_items: toLineItems(cart) },
  { idempotencyKey: key },
);
```

> [!WARNING] Never create the order on the success redirect. Order state changes only in the signed webhook.

## Why it's written this way
- The idempotency key is built from the cart's id and version, so a retried request can't charge twice.
- The webhook handler checks the signature before reading the body.
- Order state changes only in the webhook, never on the redirect.

## Common mistakes
- Creating the order on the success redirect. A closed tab loses it.
- Reusing one key for a changed cart.

entries.title: When a locked test outlives the plan
entries.description: A locked test written from an older brief fails a correct build. Escalate a test dispute instead of retrying.
entries.source: Closeout lesson from Spring launch site, M4 (parked after retry 3)
entries.content:
## The signal
The same locked test fails on two vendors, and the failure matches the plan's wording, not a bug.

## What to do
1. Stop retrying. A third try won't pass a test that asks for the wrong thing.
2. File a test dispute with the plan line and the test line side by side.
3. Brennan rules. Acceptance tests come to the operator.

> [!TIP] A dispute costs nothing to file. A fourth retry costs about a quarter of a module cap.

## Example
M4's test expected a captcha; the plan said honeypot. Three retries used 87% of the module cap before the dispute.

entries.title: The landing page's content model
entries.description: How the scaffold's CMS collections are laid out, and where a new section goes.
entries.source: Written up from the AVEL website project
entries.content:
## Collections
- `sections/` one file per page section, ordered by `order`.
- `plans/` the pricing plans, with `price` in cents.

## The schema
```ts src/content/config.ts
const plans = defineCollection({
  schema: z.object({
    name: z.string(),
    price: z.number().int(), // cents, never a float
    features: z.array(z.string()),
  }),
});
```

## Adding a section
1. Add a file in `sections/` with a new `order`.
2. Add its component in `src/components/sections/`.
3. The page picks it up; no route change.

> [!TIP] Reordering the page is a content change: edit `order` in the section's file. No build, no PR.

entries.title: How the library works
entries.description: What the agents learn from, how an entry reaches them, and how to change one.
entries.content:
## What's in it
The library holds three kinds of thing. **Knowledge** is what an agent reads: worked examples, patterns, correction pairs, checklists, lessons, decision records and domain facts. **Skills** teach an agent how to do one kind of work. **Rules** are checks that must pass.

## Entry types
| Type | What it holds | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| Worked example | Real code that passed, explained | Builders |
| Pattern | When to reach for an approach, and its cost | Builders, Canon |
| Correction pair | What failed, what passed, and why | Builders, reviewers |
| Checklist | What a reviewer checks, item by item | Reviewers |
| Lesson | Something the factory learned the hard way | Everyone |
| Decision record | A choice made once, so no one asks again | Canon, builders |
| Domain fact | A client's words, rules and history | Canon, builders |

## Layers
- **Global:** works for any stack and any client.
- **Stack:** one language or framework, such as Astro or React.
- **Client:** one client's language, rules and past decisions. It never reaches another client's projects.
- **Template:** how a template's scaffold works. Builders, test writers and Canon pull it on projects built from that template.

## How an entry reaches an agent
1. Code picks entries for each task doc by work kind, stack, domain and client, within a fixed token budget.
2. Agents can also search the library while they work. Every search is logged.
3. A project pins one knowledge release when it's finalized, and keeps it until it closes.

## Changing an entry
1. Open the entry and choose **Propose a change**.
2. Edit it, review the diff, and file the factory PR.
3. The PR waits for you in Decisions. Merging it adds the change to the next knowledge release.

## Where new entries come from
Retry pairs, review findings fixed with a regression test, searches that found nothing, and reasons you give more than once. They arrive in Decisions as candidates, never straight into the library.

## What an entry looks like
```yaml knowledge/stripe-checkout.yaml
slug: stripe-checkout
type: worked-example
layer: stack
stack: next
roles: [builder, unit-test-writer, security-reviewer]
version: 4.0.0
```

entries.title: Commit convention
entries.description: How every commit is written: the type, the first word, the scope and the trailers. Version 1.1 is proposed.
entries.content:
## The shape
Every commit, yours, an agent's or the integrator's, is written the same way. Receipts and audit read it, the contract version comes from it, and release notes are built from it.

```text commit message
type(scope)!: verb + what changes, 72 characters or less

Why this change. Wrap at 100 characters.

Checked: how it was proven
Trailer-Key: value
```

## Picking the type
Ask one question: **would the person using it notice?**

| Notice? | Type | Release note | Contract version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Yes, something new | `feat` | Added | minor |
| Yes, something broken now works | `fix` | Fixed | patch |
| Yes, it's faster or lighter | `perf` | Faster | patch |
| Yes, an earlier change is undone | `revert` | Undone | patch |
| No, cleaner code, same behavior | `refactor` | Hidden | none |
| No, tests, docs, build or CI | `test`, `docs`, `build`, `ci` | Hidden | none |
| Still no fit | `chore`, with a line saying why | Hidden | none |

A `!` after the scope makes it **Breaking**: the contract goes up a major version, and the `BREAKING CHANGE:` line becomes the note.

> [!WARNING]
> `chore` is refused on mission branches, and a `refactor` may not change a locked test's expectations. If behavior changed, it's a `fix` or a `feat`.

## The first word
Imperative and lowercase, from this list: `add`, `remove`, `show`, `hide`, `let`, `stop`, `keep`, `refuse`, `allow`, `require`, `rename`, `move`, `split`, `merge`, `replace`, `speed up`, `bump`, `document`, `test`, `revert`.

```diff
- feat(web/release): receipt page
+ feat(web/release): show the proof check on the receipt
- fix(server/gate): override bug
+ fix(server/gate): refuse an override on gate 5
- chore(M3): cleanup
+ refactor(M3): split the price rule loader
```

IDs, file names and ticket numbers go in trailers, never in the summary.

## Scopes
| Scope | After the slash |
| --- | --- |
| `web`, `server` | The module: `web/decisions`, `server/gate` |
| `contract`, `db`, `cli`, `mock` | Nothing: the package alone |
| `design`, `docs`, `repo`, `deps` | Nothing |
| `M1`, `M2`, … | Mission branches only |
| Factory repo | `skills`, `kb`, `rules`, `templates`, `roster`, `factory-yaml`, `canon` |

## Trailers
| Trailer | Meaning | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Checked` | How it was proven: `vitest web/decisions`, `manual on iPhone 15` | You on `feat`, `fix`, `perf`; the runner on agent commits |
| `Project-Kind` | `client` or `internal` | The runner and integrator |
| `Reverts` | The SHA being undone | Whoever reverts |
| `Refs`, `Closes`, `Finding` | A CR, doc or finding | Anyone |
| `Mission`, `Module`, `Agent`, `Dispatch`, `Attempt`, `Factory-Commit` | Where the commit came from | The runner, automatically |
| `Task`, `Requirement`, `Scenario` | What the agent served | The agent |

## Internal and client projects
Canon's first question decides it.

| | Client project | Internal project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Convention | The client's own, if their repo has one, plus our trailers | Always this one |
| `Project-Kind` | `client` | `internal` |
| Release notes | Offered to the client at delivery | For you only |

## Examples
```text Your commit (squashed PR)
feat(web/decisions): show what changed when an approval is stale

A 409 now refetches the decision and shows the new version beside the one
you opened, instead of a generic error.

Checked: mock, stale-version scenario
Refs: CR-W2
```

```text An agent's commit on a mission branch
feat(M2): let customers request a quote from the landing page

Task: M2-T3
Requirement: R7
Scenario: S12
Checked: 6 locked tests pass
Project-Kind: client
Mission: gts-landing
Module: M2
Agent: Leon
Dispatch: D-42
Attempt: a2
Factory-Commit: 4e1c9a0
```

```text A revert
revert(web/kit): bring back the old button height

Reverts: 4e1c9a0
Checked: screenshot matrix
```

## How it's enforced
| Where | How |
| --- | --- |
| Your machine | commitlint in the `commit-msg` hook that `avel link` installs |
| Pull requests | CI checks the PR title; merges are squash only |
| Agent attempts | The `commits:` rule in `avel check`, rules version 14; Gate 3 fails a badly formed commit |
| Integration commits | The integrator writes them from the module's goal and its trailers |
history: Proposed: one question picks the type, a verb list, Checked and Project-Kind trailers, no chore on mission branches

entries.title: Annual prices apply the discount
entries.description: The annual price is the monthly price × 12 minus the plan's annual discount, rounded once.
entries.source: Review finding F-6 on Spring launch site, M2
entries.content:
## Before
```ts
annual = monthly * 12
```

## After
```ts
annual = Math.round(monthly * 12 * (1 - plan.annualDiscount))
```

## Why
The pricing table showed the monthly figure × 12, so annual plans looked more expensive than they were. Round once, at the end, so cents don't drift.

entries.title: Use Intl, not a date library
entries.description: Format and compare dates with the platform's Intl and Temporal APIs. Date libraries are refused.
entries.source: Your reasons on three dependency requests
entries.content:
## Decision
Builders format dates with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and compare them with `Temporal` where it's available. Requests for dayjs, date-fns or luxon are refused.

## Why
- The platform covers every case the factory has met so far.
- One fewer dependency per project, and one fewer way to get time zones wrong.

## Background
Refused three times, on three projects, with the same reason. Repeated reasons become decision records.

entries.title: Check the budget before retry 2
entries.description: Retry 2 costs about as much as the first attempt. If the module has less than that left, ask first.
entries.source: Closeout lesson from Spring launch site, M3
entries.content:
## The signal
A module on retry 1 with less than a quarter of its cap left.

## What happens without it
Retry 2 starts, hits the module cap halfway, and parks. You pay for half a retry and still get a parked proposal.

## What to do
The scheduler raises a budget proposal before retry 2 when the remaining budget is under one attempt cap.

entries.title: Split modules along file territories
entries.description: Modules that run at the same time never share files. Split by territory, not by feature words.
entries.content:
## When to use it
At checkpoint 0.2, when Canon breaks a project into modules.

## The pattern
- Give each module its own folders to write in.
- Put shared types in the foundation module, M0, so later modules only read them.
- If two modules must touch one file, make one depend on the other.

## In the plan
```yaml plan.yaml
modules:
  - ref: M0
    owns: [src/lib/types/, src/styles/]
  - ref: M2
    owns: [src/components/pricing/]
    after: [M0]   # reads the shared types, never writes them
```

## Trade-offs
More dependencies mean fewer modules run at once. Gate 1 refuses overlapping territories, so the trade is made at planning time, not at merge time.

entries.title: How Harbor Dental books appointments
entries.description: Slots, holds and reminders, in Harbor Dental's own words.
entries.content:
## Words
- **Slot:** 30 minutes on one chair.
- **Hold:** a slot kept for 90 seconds while someone books it.
- **Recall:** a check-up booked six months ahead.

## Rules
- A patient can hold one slot at a time.
- Reminders go out 48 hours and 2 hours before.

entries.title: React and TanStack performance
entries.description: Waterfalls, bundle size and re-renders in React 19 with TanStack Router and Query.
entries.content:
---
name: react-tanstack-performance
description: Keep React and TanStack apps fast: no request waterfalls, small bundles, few re-renders.
---

1. Load route data in the loader, in parallel.
2. Split by route; never import a whole icon set.
3. Derive state during render instead of syncing it in an effect.
